S&P 500 (+0.44% to 7746.18): Tech Stocks Drive S&P 500 Gains. The S&P 500 rose 0.44% to 7746.18 as tech stocks rebounded, driven by optimism about the start of the Q3 earnings season. This rebound was fueled by the resurgence of AI trade, which has been making a comeback. As a result, traders are watching the performance of tech-heavy stocks such as those mentioned in the headlines.
Nasdaq (+0.99% to 26687.74): Nasdaq Tech Stocks Rebound. The Nasdaq's 0.99% rise was driven by optimism in tech stocks, with investors looking forward to the week's earnings season and potential deals in the space, including a reported Tesla-SpaceX partnership. [7] [4] [6] [5] [7] [1] [2] [3]
10-Year Yield (-0.04% to 5.12): Yields Fall Amid Calming Bond Market. The 10-year yield fell 0.04% to 5.12 as the bond market calmed down, with traders breathing a sigh of relief after a period of volatility. [8] The WSJ reported that French government-bond yields rose on protests and budget concerns, but Treasury yields fell instead, suggesting a shift in market sentiment. [10] CNBC attributed the move to weak housing data, which may have reduced investor appetite for risk. [11]
USD/JPY (-0.3% to 158.05): USD/JPY Sell-Off. The USD/JPY pair fell 0.3% to 158.05 as investors took profits from a recent rally, citing a record Japanese bond auction that sparked a Yen rally [12]. Traders are watching the Yen's performance, as a strong auction could lead to higher interest rates in Japan, making the Yen more attractive [13]. The narrow trading range in the pair, as seen in the latest comments from UOB, also contributed to the sell-off [15].
Crude Oil (-4.02% to 97.7): Oil Price Drop Sparks Market Reaction. Crude oil fell 4.02% to 97.7 as traders reassessed the market's reaction to the recent developments in the Middle East, particularly the hopes of diplomatic progress between Iran and other countries. The jump in oil prices earlier in the day, driven by concerns about potential supply disruptions, was reversed as traders weighed the recovery of Gulf supply. The decline in oil prices also led to a drop in gold prices, with investors growing more concerned about inflation fears.
Gold (+0.1% to 4146.6): Gold Prices Rise Amid Inflation Fears. Gold prices rose 0.1% to 4146.6 as traders watched oil prices rise, sparking concerns about inflation. Despite falling yields, gold was pressured by elevated oil prices, which led to a near one-week low. The market is also closely watching the ongoing Hormuz diplomacy, which has sparked a reversal in oil prices, according to Reuters [22].
